# Circles and Paths

#### Course: Canvas Foundations

## Circles and Paths

Rectangles are drawn in a single call. Circles work a little differently.

To draw a circle on canvas you use something called a path. A path is an invisible shape you define first, then render. It sounds like extra work but it is actually simple once you see it.

```html
1<!DOCTYPE html>
2<html lang="en">
3    <head>
4        <meta charset="UTF-8">
5        <title>Canvas</title>
6        <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
7    </head>
8    <body>
9        <canvas id="gameCanvas" width="400" height="300">
10        </canvas>
11        <script src="script.js">
12        </script>
13    </body>
14</html>
```

```css
1*  {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6body  {
7    display: flex;
8    justify-content: center;
9    align-items: center;
10    height: 100vh;
11    background: #f0f0f0;
12}
13canvas  {
14    display: block;
15    border: 1px solid #ccc;
16    background: #fff;
17}
```

```javascript
1const canvas = document.getElementById("gameCanvas");
2const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
3ctx.beginPath();
4ctx.arc(200, 150, 10, 0, Math.PI * 2);
5ctx.fill();
```

Here, beginPath() tells the canvas to start a fresh path. arc(x, y, radius, startAngle, endAngle) defines a circle centered at (200, 150) with radius 10. The angles are in radians - 0 to Math.PI * 2 is a full circle. Then fill() paints the shape solid.

The arc syntax looks like this:

```javascriptDOM
ctx.arc(x, y, radius, startAngle, endAngle);
```

Always call beginPath() before drawing a new shape. Without it, the canvas keeps adding to the existing path. I have hit this bug more times than I want to admit - you draw a second circle without beginPath() and suddenly the first one gets redrawn in the wrong color. One beginPath() at the start of each shape saves a lot of debugging.
